resources.string: Your controls for both screens live here. Press the AYN button to open or close it. First, make it yours, then a few things that are easy to miss. Press A for next, B to go back, and Y to skip.
Press and hold anywhere on the panel to start arranging its cards. Try it now.
Drag a card onto another card or an empty spot to move it. You can drag the nav bar to the top or bottom, too.
Tap Done to keep it, or Reset to go back to the default layout.
Tap a preset to restyle the panel and see the difference. The companion\'s Themes section has the full list, and you can mix your own there.
This button opens an app of your choice on the screen you pick. Choose the app in the companion under Nav Bar → Quick Launch. Until you do, it stays hidden.

Play GIF and animated WebP background images and let gradient backgrounds move (both set in Appearance). An animated background uses more battery while the panel is open. While this is off, an animated image shows its first frame and a gradient shows still.

Put a dot on settings that are new after an update. Turning this off only hides the dots: anything you haven\'t seen yet shows again when you turn it back on.

Open the overlay on the bottom screen to preview your settings.
Continuously keep the last few seconds of the screen in memory so you can save a clip after something happens. Uses root screen capture (no cast prompt).
Record what you hear, while it keeps playing. Some apps block recording, so their clips are silent.
Mix your voice into clips. Android shows the mic indicator while the buffer is on.
The root helper isn\'t running, so clips will have no sound. The Replay Buffer also needs it to record the screen. Run the checks in Diagnostics to start it again.

TCP SC (TCP Save Clip) is a shortcut for Replay Buffer: opening it saves a clip, or turns the buffer on if it\'s off. Open it from anything that can launch an app, like a home screen shortcut, a gesture app or Back Button Hero. Launch it on the bottom screen so your game keeps focus.
Installed, but it can\'t save clips yet. Reinstall it so Android lets it talk to Command Panel.
This is a debug build: it only works with a TCP SC you build yourself, so installing from GitHub is off here.
Its own app, used as a panel plugin.
ThorKBM turns the bottom screen into a keyboard and trackpad for the top screen. Install it here once; after that it keeps itself up to date.
ThorKBM on the bottom screen: a keyboard with a trackpad beside it

This quick tour goes through each section of the companion and what it controls. Press A for the next step, B to go back, and Y to skip.

Settings are split into sections here. General sits on top, and the rest are gathered into groups you can open and close. Moving through the list switches the pane on the right, and D-pad Right jumps into that section\'s settings.\n\nYou can rearrange the list too: a later step shows how.

Related sections share a group. Moving onto a group doesn\'t change the pane: open it to reach its sections, and press A on a section to go into it. With touch, tap a group to open or close it, and drag a handle to move a group or a section.
Open or close a group. D-pad Right and Left work too.
On a group: pick it up, move it with the D-pad, then press A, Y or B to drop it.
On a section: pick it up, move it within its group, then press A, Y or B to drop it.
Core behavior: updates, taking over the AYN button, status bar extras, new dots and backups.
Turn this on so the AYN button opens Command Panel\'s overlay instead of the built-in dual-screen assistant. Turning it off gives the button back.
Fine-tune the overlay: show a battery time estimate, hide the network speed readout, and choose which apps Clear All Tasks leaves running.
After an update, a dot marks each new setting until you\'ve seen it. Turn this off to hide the dots. Anything you haven\'t seen yet shows again when you turn it back on.
Save every companion setting to a JSON file, or restore your most recent backup after a reinstall.
See which version you\'re on, check for a new release and reopen the patch notes. Command Panel downloads and installs updates itself.

Keep the last few seconds in memory, then save a clip after something happens. Capture the top screen, the bottom one, or both stacked into one video, and pick how far back it reaches, the clip quality and where clips go. Auto-delete old clips can remove clips by age or total size so they don\'t fill your storage.
Everything for your clips: Replay Studio to watch them, the buffer itself, TCP SC to save clips from a shortcut, the double press, audio, auto-delete and where clips go.
Shows your newest clip and how many you have. Open Replay Studio to watch, trim, share and delete clips. Turn on Play on the recorded screen to play bottom-screen clips on the lower screen.

TCP SC is a shortcut for Replay Buffer: open it from a home screen shortcut, a gesture or an app like Back Button Hero to save a clip. This shows whether TCP SC is installed, and installs the one that matches your version of Command Panel.
Open the overlay on the bottom screen to try your changes for real.
Arrange the buttons along the bottom of the overlay and set up a Quick Launch shortcut.
Put the nav bar buttons in the order you want. With a controller, press A to pick one up, move it with the D-pad, and press A again to drop it.

Add a Launch button that opens an app of your choice on the screen you pick. Once you choose an app, pick what the panel does after launching: close, stay open, or come back when you leave the app. The button can show the app\'s icon and name, too.
Choose which tiles the overlay shows and the order they appear in.
Show icons only for a cleaner grid. The icons grow to fill the space.
Your enabled tiles in overlay order. Drag them, or use A and the D-pad, to rearrange them.
Every tile Command Panel offers, grouped into the stock AYN tiles, Android system tiles and extra tools. Flip a switch to add or remove a tile.
The overlay\'s theme mode, and how its look and accent carry over to this screen.
Light, dark, or follow the system theme for the bottom-screen overlay.
Make your own gradient backgrounds and keep them in a library. Apply one to show it behind the panel on any look, or switch back to your image.
Restyle this companion screen with the overlay\'s look, theme and accent, so both screens match.
Use the Thor\'s Ambient LED color as the overlay\'s accent, so the UI matches your joystick lights.
Pick a look for the overlay, mix your own in Theme Studio, and share or download looks.
The look the overlay uses right now, previewed live. Customize opens it in Theme Studio.
Start a new look in Theme Studio by combining cards, tiles, gauges, sliders, nav and fonts from any look.
Looks you\'ve saved. Export them as a pack to share, or import a pack someone sent you.
Packs you put in the TCP Themes folder show up here, along with the fonts they use.
Follow a GitHub theme repo or a link to a pack. Its looks are added and stay up to date as the author changes them.
Command Panel follows the TCP Themes repo from the start, so new looks show up on their own as they\'re added. Find them under Themes → Packs, or remove the repo here if you\'d rather not.
All the looks that ship with Command Panel. Pick one to apply it to the overlay right away.
Get ThorKBM, the keyboard and trackpad app for the Thor, and choose whether the panel shows its nav bar button and Keyboard tile.
Install ThorKBM here once and it keeps itself up to date. After that, the card shows which version you have, and Open starts it.
Check that the privileged access Command Panel relies on is working.
Checks hidden-API access, the root shell and the root helper. If a feature isn\'t working, start here.
Features still being tested, like In-game FPS. They may change, or not work perfectly yet.
That\'s the tour. Take it again any time from General → Updates.
A quick tour of this version\'s changes, one stop each.
For a tour of everything, go to General → Updates and choose Take the tour.

Turn this on to use GIF and animated WebP backgrounds. They play only while the panel is open.
